title: All-Time Great Indian Spy & Espionage Films
description: 20 gripping Indian films about intelligence agents, undercover missions, infiltration, counter-terrorism, surveillance and the dangerous world of secrets and deception.

entries.why_it_ranks: Meghna Gulzar strips espionage of glamour and makes Sehmat's undercover mission psychologically and emotionally costly, with Alia Bhatt delivering an exceptional performance.
A sprawling undercover espionage-action drama built around infiltration into Karachi's criminal and terror networks, combining intelligence operations with crime and large-scale action.
One of India's most grounded geopolitical thrillers, treating intelligence work, civil war and political assassination with unusual seriousness.
Neeraj Pandey presents intelligence work as patient surveillance, information gathering and precise operations rather than nonstop superheroics.
Kamal Haasan combines espionage, terrorism and international action with an ambitious narrative and one of his most memorable transformations.
Indian intelligence agents attempting to extract a major fugitive from Pakistan produces a tense mission film with unusually high emotional stakes.
Adivi Sesh helped modernize Telugu spy cinema with a tightly constructed story of recruitment, betrayal, identity and intelligence operations.
Kabir Khan successfully combines RAW-ISI espionage with mainstream romance and action while establishing one of modern Hindi cinema's defining spy characters.
Uneven but ambitious, with Sriram Raghavan attempting an international old-school espionage adventure rather than a conventional Bollywood action film.
Vishal Bhardwaj takes a quieter approach to espionage, focusing on betrayal, surveillance, divided loyalties and the personal lives destroyed by intelligence work.
More action-heavy than espionage-heavy, but its multinational rescue mission expands the scale of Indian spy cinema considerably.
An unusual attempt to show the recruitment and development of an intelligence operative rather than beginning with an already invincible agent.
An underrated story about an informer repeatedly infiltrating dangerous organizations and paying a heavy psychological price for living under false identities.
A RAW operative infiltrating Pakistan before the 1971 war provides a more traditional undercover-espionage narrative centred on identity and sacrifice.
A hijacking crisis provides the framework for an old-fashioned intelligence mission built around investigation, planning and covert intervention.
An undercover RAW operative living inside Pakistan gives the film a classic espionage setup involving false identity, intelligence gathering and divided personal loyalties.

film.title: The Hero: Love Story of a Spy

entries.why_it_ranks: Excessive but historically interesting as one of Bollywood's major early attempts at mounting a large-scale international spy blockbuster.
A mainstream Telugu attempt to combine intelligence operations, national-security conspiracy and action within a contemporary spy framework.
Much more action spectacle than realistic espionage, but its enormous popularity made the modern Indian cinematic spy universe a major mainstream phenomenon.
Again action-first, but rogue agents, intelligence operations, deception and Hrithik Roshan-Tiger Shroff star power make it an important modern spy entertainer.
